## Label self-consistency

Carried over from `DiffuChannel_analysis.Rmd`, where it ran on one record at a
time. Each arm's current trace is idealised on its own, with a conventional
half-amplitude criterion and no reference to any other arm, and the result is
compared against the `Channels` column that arm shipped with.

This asks a different question from everything above. The GAN emitted its labels
and its trace together, so there is no external truth to score them against --
but there is an internal one: the labels should agree with what the arm's own
current is doing. The diffusion arm was handed its labels before it started, so
its agreement measures whether the generated current followed the conditioning
it was given. The real record supplies the floor, because expert idealisation
and a half-amplitude criterion do not agree perfectly either, and an arm cannot
reasonably be asked to do better than the seed.

```{r self-consistency}
res_selfcon <- purrr::map(manifest$phenotype, function(ph) {

  arms <- recs[[ph]]
  fs   <- FS_MAIN[[ph]]

  # First pass: try unsupervised EM on every arm.
  em_rec <- purrr::map(names(arms), function(a) {

    d <- arms[[a]]

    n_lev <- max(
      1,
      max(d$channels, na.rm = TRUE)
    )

    idealise_half_amplitude(
      d$current,
      n_levels = n_lev,
      polarity = POL_MAIN[[ph]]
    )
  })

  names(em_rec) <- names(arms)

  # If EM fails for any arm, use label-anchored CV for every
  # arm in this phenotype, keeping the comparison consistent.
  em_failed <- vapply(
    em_rec,
    function(x) all(is.na(x)),
    logical(1)
  )

  phenotype_fallback <- any(em_failed)

  if (phenotype_fallback) {
    failed_arms <- names(arms)[em_failed]

    method_note <- paste0(
      "Phenotype-wide fallback because unsupervised EM failed for: ",
      paste(failed_arms, collapse = ", ")
    )
  } else {
    method_note <- ""
  }

  # Second pass: calculate self-consistency using the method
  # selected for this entire phenotype.
  out <- purrr::map(names(arms), function(a) {

    d <- arms[[a]]

    n_lev <- max(
      1,
      max(d$channels, na.rm = TRUE)
    )

    lab <- d$channels > 0

    if (phenotype_fallback) {

      rec <- idealise_label_anchored_cv(
        current = d$current,
        labels = d$channels,
        n_levels = n_lev,
        polarity = POL_MAIN[[ph]],
        block_len = 1000L,
        trim = 0.10,
        min_state_n = 50L
      )

      ideal_method <- "Phenotype-wide label-anchored CV fallback"

    } else {

      rec <- em_rec[[a]]
      ideal_method <- "Unsupervised EM"
    }

    # This occurs only if the selected phenotype-wide
    # method still fails for this arm.
    if (all(is.na(rec))) {

      failure_reason <- attr(rec, "why")

      if (is.null(failure_reason)) {
        failure_reason <- "no reason was recorded"
      }

      return(list(
        summary = tibble::tibble(
          phenotype = ph,
          source = a,
          kappa = NA_real_,
          f1_open = NA_real_,
          popen_labels = mean(lab),
          popen_recovered = NA_real_,
          open_ms_labels = NA_real_,
          open_ms_recovered = NA_real_,
          flicker = NA,
          ideal_method = ideal_method,
          note = paste(
            method_note,
            "Selected method failed:",
            failure_reason
          )
        ),
        dwell = NULL
      ))
    }

    op <- rec > 0

    tp <- sum(lab & op)
    fp <- sum(!lab & op)
    fn <- sum(lab & !op)

    dl <- dwell_times(
      as.integer(lab),
      fs[[a]]
    )

    dr <- dwell_times(
      as.integer(op),
      fs[[a]]
    )

    mo <- function(x) {

      v <- x$dwell_ms[x$state == "Open"]

      if (length(v)) {
        mean(v)
      } else {
        NA_real_
      }
    }

    list(
      summary = tibble::tibble(
        phenotype = ph,
        source = a,
        kappa = cohen_kappa(lab, op),
        f1_open = if (2 * tp + fp + fn > 0) {
          2 * tp / (2 * tp + fp + fn)
        } else {
          NA_real_
        },
        popen_labels = mean(lab),
        popen_recovered = mean(op),
        open_ms_labels = mo(dl),
        open_ms_recovered = mo(dr),
        flicker = length(rle(op)$lengths) > 0.5 * length(op),
        ideal_method = ideal_method,
        note = method_note
      ),

      dwell = dplyr::bind_rows(
        dplyr::mutate(
          dl,
          origin = "Own labels"
        ),
        dplyr::mutate(
          dr,
          origin = "Recovered from current"
        )
      ) |>
        dplyr::mutate(
          phenotype = ph,
          source = a
        )
    )
  })

  list(
    summary = purrr::map_dfr(out, "summary"),
    dwell   = purrr::map_dfr(out, "dwell")
  )
})

self_consist <- purrr::map_dfr(res_selfcon, "summary")
sc_dwell     <- purrr::map_dfr(res_selfcon, "dwell")

if (any(self_consist$flicker %in% TRUE)) {
  warning("The recovered idealisation switches on more than half the samples ",
          "in: ", paste(sprintf("%s/%s", self_consist$phenotype[self_consist$flicker %in% TRUE],
                                self_consist$source[self_consist$flicker %in% TRUE]),
                        collapse = ", "),
          ". That is a wrong level estimate rather than a fast record, and the ",
          "kappa for those rows means nothing. Check the amplitude histogram.")
}

# A recovered Popen that is the complement of the labelled one is an inverted
# idealisation, not a disagreement, and its kappa is the negative of the real
# number. It should not happen now the polarity is imposed, so say so loudly.
inverted <- self_consist |>
  dplyr::filter(is.finite(kappa),
                abs(popen_recovered - (1 - popen_labels)) < 0.05,
                kappa < 0)
if (nrow(inverted)) {
  warning("The idealisation looks inverted in: ",
          paste(sprintf("%s/%s", inverted$phenotype, inverted$source),
                collapse = ", "), ". Check POL_MAIN for those phenotypes.")
}

nice_kable(self_consist, digits = 4,
             caption = paste("Label self-consistency. Each arm's",
                             "Channels column against a half-amplitude",
                             "idealisation of that same arm's current. The real",
                             "record is the floor, not a target of 1."))

sc_cmp <- self_consist |>
  dplyr::select(phenotype, source, kappa) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = source, values_from = kappa) |>
  dplyr::filter(
    is.finite(Real),
    is.finite(Diffusion),
    is.finite(GAN)
  ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
  deficit_diffusion = Real - Diffusion,
  deficit_gan       = Real - GAN,

  error_diffusion = abs(Diffusion - Real),
  error_gan       = abs(GAN - Real),

  pct_error_diffusion = 100 * error_diffusion / abs(Real),
  pct_error_gan       = 100 * error_gan / abs(Real),

  favours = dplyr::case_when(
    error_diffusion < error_gan ~ "Diffusion",
    error_gan < error_diffusion ~ "GAN",
    TRUE                        ~ "Tie"
  )
)

nice_kable(sc_cmp, digits = 4,
             caption = paste("Shortfall in kappa against the real",
                             "record's own floor. A negative deficit means the",
                             "arm's labels agree with its current better than",
                             "the expert idealisation agrees with the seed,",
                             "which is a sign the arm is too clean rather than",
                             "a sign it is good."))

cat(sprintf("\nPhenotypes where the diffusion arm is the more self-consistent: %d of %d.\n",
            sum(sc_cmp$favours == "Diffusion"), nrow(sc_cmp)))

readr::write_csv(self_consist, file.path(CFG$out_dir, "self_consistency.csv"))
readr::write_csv(sc_cmp, file.path(CFG$out_dir, "self_consistency_comparison.csv"))
```

The gap between the two dwell distributions below is the missed-event loss: the
brief openings and closures that a half-amplitude criterion cannot recover from
the current, however good the trace is. Being able to measure it at all is what
having the conditioning idealisation buys.

```{r fig-selfcon, fig.width = 10, fig.height = 7}
pal_origin <- c("Own labels" = "#1b1b1b",
                "Recovered from current" = "#c0392b")

d_sc <- sc_dwell |>
  dplyr::filter(dwell_ms > 0) |>
  dplyr::mutate(source = factor(source, levels = c("Real", "Diffusion", "GAN")),
                origin = factor(origin, levels = names(pal_origin)))

brk_sc <- 10^seq(log10(min(d_sc$dwell_ms)), log10(max(d_sc$dwell_ms)),
                 length.out = 41)

p_selfcon <- ggplot(d_sc, aes(dwell_ms, colour = origin)) +
  geom_histogram(aes(y = after_stat(sqrt(count)), fill = origin),
                 breaks = brk_sc, alpha = 0.15, position = "identity",
                 colour = NA) +
  geom_histogram(aes(y = after_stat(sqrt(count))), fill = NA,
                 breaks = brk_sc, linewidth = 0.4, position = "identity") +
  facet_grid(
    phenotype ~ source + state,
    scales = "free_y",
    labeller = labeller(
      phenotype = function(x) gsub("_", "\n", x, fixed = TRUE)
    )
  ) +
  scale_x_log10(labels = scales::label_number()) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = pal_origin) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = pal_origin, guide = "none") +
  labs(x = "Dwell time (ms)", y = expression(sqrt(count))) +
  theme_channel() +
  theme(
    strip.text.y = element_text(
      angle = 270,
      hjust = 0.5,
      vjust = 0.5
    )
  ) +
  guides(
    colour = guide_legend(
      override.aes = list(
        fill = scales::alpha(pal_origin, 0.15),
        linewidth = 0.4
      )
    )
  )

p_selfcon

save_fig(p_selfcon, "fig_self_consistency", width = 10, height = 1.5 * n_ph + 1)
readr::write_csv(sc_dwell, file.path(CFG$out_dir, "self_consistency_dwells.csv"))
```

## Dwell time constants

Section 3.6 of the manuscript asks for exponential time constants, not mean
dwells. Both are fitted here from the same two dwell sets the self-consistency
step already produces: the arm's own labels, which for the diffusion arm are
the exact conditioning ground truth, and the idealisation recovered from that
arm's current by a half-amplitude criterion. The difference between them is the
missed-event loss.

Where the column reports one component, two could not be supported and the mean
dwell is the only defensible summary for that row. That is a property of the
record, not a failure of the fit: a phenotype whose closed dwells average three
or four samples has no exponential structure left to resolve.

```{r dwell-tau}
tau_fits <- sc_dwell |>
  dplyr::group_by(phenotype, source, state, origin) |>
  dplyr::group_modify(~ fit_exp_mixture(.x$dwell_ms)) |>
  dplyr::ungroup() |>
  dplyr::mutate(origin = dplyr::recode(origin,
                  `Own labels` = "true",
                  `Recovered from current` = "recovered"))

nice_kable(tau_fits, digits = 4,
           caption = paste("Dwell time constants. 'true' is the arm's own",
                           "label column, which for the diffusion arm is the",
                           "conditioning ground truth; 'recovered' is the",
                           "idealisation recovered from that arm's current.",
                           "n_components is 1 where a two-component fit could",
                           "not be supported."))

readr::write_csv(tau_fits, file.path(CFG$out_dir, "dwell_tau_fits.csv"))

cat(sprintf(
  "\nTwo-component fits supportable in %d of %d phenotype/state/origin cells.\n",
  sum(tau_fits$n_components == 2), nrow(tau_fits)))
```

The density above says whether the envelope has the right spread; it says
nothing about whether it wanders on the right timescale, because a distribution
has no time axis. The panel below is the envelope as a time course, which is
what the manuscript's Figure 4A shows. It was previously produced only by

## Cluster separation of the projections

The projections above are judged by eye, which is not a measurement. This tests
whether the real and synthetic point clouds are separable in the embedding,
using the permutation approach of ClusterSignificance as in the DeepGANnel
paper. A *large* p is the favourable outcome here: it means the two clouds
cannot be told apart, which is the opposite of the usual reading and is worth
stating explicitly in the legend.

The test is run within a phenotype and within a projection method, since the
coordinates of one embedding mean nothing in another.

```{r cluster-test, eval = CFG$do_manifold && isTRUE(CFG$do_cluster_test)}
if (!requireNamespace("ClusterSignificance", quietly = TRUE)) {
  message("ClusterSignificance is not installed, so [[cluster_p]] cannot be ",
          "filled. It is a Bioconductor package:\n",
          '  BiocManager::install("ClusterSignificance")\n',
          "Either install it, or delete the ClusterSignificance sentence and ",
          "reference [49] from Methods 2.9 and the claim from Section 3.8.")
  cluster_tbl <- NULL
} else {
  # pcp() takes a two-column matrix and a grouping factor and returns a
  # p-value for every pairwise group comparison, so one call per phenotype
  # per method covers both Real-vs-Diffusion and Real-vs-GAN.
  cluster_one <- function(d) {
    mat <- as.matrix(d[, c("x", "y")])
    grp <- factor(as.character(d$source))
    if (dplyr::n_distinct(grp) < 2 || nrow(mat) < 10) return(NULL)
    pe <- ClusterSignificance::permute(
      mat = mat, groups = grp, iter = CFG$n_perm_cluster, projmethod = "pcp")
    p <- ClusterSignificance::pvalue(pe)
    tibble::tibble(comparison = names(p), p = as.numeric(p))
  }

  cluster_tbl <- proj |>
    dplyr::group_by(phenotype, method) |>
    dplyr::group_modify(~ {
      r <- tryCatch(cluster_one(.x),
                    error = function(e)
                      tibble::tibble(comparison = "failed",
                                     p = NA_real_,
                                     note = conditionMessage(e)))
      if (is.null(r)) tibble::tibble(comparison = NA_character_, p = NA_real_) else r
    }) |>
    dplyr::ungroup()

  nice_kable(cluster_tbl, digits = 4,
             caption = paste("ClusterSignificance permutation p-values for",
                             "separation between the point clouds in each",
                             "embedding. A large p means the clouds are not",
                             "separable, which is the favourable result."))

  readr::write_csv(cluster_tbl,
                   file.path(CFG$out_dir, "cluster_significance.csv"))

  if (any(is.na(cluster_tbl$p)))
    warning("Some cluster tests returned no p-value. Read the note column ",
            "before quoting anything from this table.")
}
```

## Figure: generation block joins

Long records are assembled from overlapping blocks bridged by context-carry
inpainting, so the one artefact this pipeline could plausibly introduce is a
seam. If the inpainting works, the distribution of sample-to-sample differences
in the neighbourhood of a join is indistinguishable from that within a block.
If it does not, it shows up here rather than in review.

This ran per record in `DiffuChannel_analysis.Rmd` and is done here for every
phenotype, on the **uncropped** diffusion arm, since cropping would move the
joins. Only the diffusion arm has joins at all: the GAN emits a record in one
pass and the seed record was never assembled from anything.

```{r fig-seams, fig.height = 7}
step <- CFG$block_len - CFG$context_len
half <- CFG$context_len %/% 2

# Joins of one record, dropping any that fall within half a context length of
# either end, where there is not enough material on both sides to compare.
joins_of <- function(n) {
  # seq() errors rather than returning nothing when the record is shorter
  # than one block, so that case is caught before it is reached.
  if (n <= step) return(numeric(0))
  b <- seq(step, n - 1L, by = step)
  b[b > CFG$context_len & b < (n - CFG$context_len)]
}

seam_one <- function(d, ph) {
  n <- nrow(d)
  b <- joins_of(n)
  diffs <- diff(d$current)

  if (!length(b)) {
    return(list(
      summary = tibble::tibble(phenotype = ph, n_samples = n, n_joins = 0L,
                               ks_seam = NA_real_, p_seam = NA_real_,
                               note = "single block, no joins to test"),
      dens = NULL, trace = NULL, joins = numeric(0)))
  }

  near <- unique(unlist(lapply(b, function(i) seq(i - half, i + half))))
  near <- near[near >= 1 & near <= length(diffs)]
  far  <- setdiff(seq_along(diffs), near)

  ks <- ks_safe(diffs[near], diffs[far])

  # The two sets are compared at equal size, so the density panel cannot be
  # read as a difference in smoothness that is really a difference in n.
  far_s <- sample(far, min(length(far), length(near)))

  # Decimated for drawing only. The statistic above uses every sample.
  dec <- max(1L, n %/% 20000L)
  keep <- seq(1L, n, by = dec)

  list(
    summary = tibble::tibble(
      phenotype = ph, n_samples = n, n_joins = length(b),
      ks_seam = unname(ks$statistic), p_seam = unname(ks$p.value),
      note = sprintf("%d samples near a join, %d within blocks",
                     length(near), length(far))),
    dens = dplyr::bind_rows(
      tibble::tibble(d = diffs[near],  where = "Near block join"),
      tibble::tibble(d = diffs[far_s], where = "Within block")) |>
      dplyr::mutate(phenotype = ph),
    trace = tibble::tibble(phenotype = ph, time_s = d$time[keep],
                           current = d$current[keep]),
    joins = d$time[b])
}

res_seam <- purrr::imap(recs_full_diffusion, function(d, ph) seam_one(d, ph))

seam_tbl   <- purrr::map_dfr(res_seam, "summary")
seam_dens  <- purrr::map_dfr(res_seam, "dens")
seam_trace <- purrr::map_dfr(res_seam, "trace")
seam_lines <- purrr::imap_dfr(res_seam, function(r, ph)
  if (length(r$joins)) tibble::tibble(phenotype = ph, time_s = r$joins) else NULL)

nice_kable(seam_tbl, digits = 4,
           caption = paste("Block joins in the diffusion arm. ks_seam compares",
                           "sample-to-sample differences within half a carried",
                           "context of a join against those within blocks. A",
                           "small statistic means the join is not detectable in",
                           "the output."))

readr::write_csv(seam_tbl, file.path(CFG$out_dir, "seam_test.csv"))
```

```{r fig-seam-panels, fig.height = 7}

  p_long <- ggplot(seam_trace, aes(time_s, current)) +

}
```

# 7. Numbers for the manuscript

Rows keyed to `[[placeholder]]` names. Pooled values are medians across
phenotypes, with the range, because five records do not support a mean and an
interval being read as an estimate.

```{r placeholders}
fmt <- function(x, d = 4) formatC(x, digits = d, format = "g")

pooled <- scored |>
  dplyr::group_by(metric, method) |>
  dplyr::summarise(median = median(value), lo = min(value), hi = max(value),
                   .groups = "drop")

placeholders <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  tibble::tibble(placeholder = "n_phenotypes", value = as.character(n_ph),
                 note = "paired seed records"),
  # Two different totals, previously conflated under one name: the seed
  # material that exists, and the subset actually scored after every arm of a
  # phenotype was cropped to its shortest. The manuscript wants the first.
  tibble::tibble(placeholder = "n_samples_total",
                 value = format(sum(seed_inventory$n_rows), big.mark = ","),
                 note = "seed samples across all phenotypes, before cropping"),
  tibble::tibble(placeholder = "n_samples_analysed",
                 value = format(sum(info$n_real), big.mark = ","),
                 note = "seed samples actually scored, after cropping each phenotype to its shortest arm"),
  # Rate before unique, or floating-point dust splits one rate into several.
  tibble::tibble(placeholder = "sample_khz",
                 value = paste(unique(round(sort(info$fs_real) / 1000, 3)),
                               collapse = ", "),
                 note = "acquisition rate(s), kHz"),
  pooled |>
    dplyr::transmute(
      placeholder = paste0(gsub("[^A-Za-z0-9]+", "_", tolower(metric)), "_",
                           tolower(method)),
      value = sprintf("%s (%s to %s)", fmt(median), fmt(lo), fmt(hi)),
      note = paste("median across phenotypes, range in brackets")),
  paired_stats |>
    dplyr::transmute(
      placeholder = paste0("unanimity_", gsub("[^A-Za-z0-9]+", "_", tolower(metric))),
      value = sprintf("%d/%d favour Diffusion", n_favour_diff, n),
      note = verdict),
  # Dwell time constants for the diffusion arm, recovered against true, over
  # the phenotypes where a two-component fit held. Reported per phenotype
  # rather than pooled: a time constant is not comparable across records the
  # way a distance is.
  {
    tf <- tau_fits |>
      dplyr::filter(source == "Diffusion", n_components == 2L)
    if (nrow(tf)) {
      tf |>
        dplyr::mutate(ph = gsub("^Phenotype_", "", phenotype)) |>
        dplyr::group_by(state, origin) |>
        dplyr::summarise(
          value = paste(sprintf("%s %.3g/%.3g", ph, tau_fast_ms, tau_slow_ms),
                        collapse = ", "),
          n_ph = dplyr::n(), .groups = "drop") |>
        dplyr::transmute(
          placeholder = sprintf("tau_%s_%s", tolower(state), origin),
          value = value,
          note = sprintf("fast/slow tau in ms, per phenotype, %d of %d phenotypes supported two components",
                         n_ph, dplyr::n_distinct(tau_fits$phenotype)))
    } else {
      tibble::tibble(placeholder = "tau_fits", value = "NOT SUPPORTED",
                     note = "no phenotype supported a two-component dwell fit")
    }
  },
  # Cluster separation, if the optional test ran.
  {
    if (exists("cluster_tbl") && !is.null(cluster_tbl) &&
        any(is.finite(cluster_tbl$p))) {
      cp <- dplyr::filter(cluster_tbl, is.finite(p))
      tibble::tibble(
        placeholder = "cluster_p",
        value = sprintf("%s (%s to %s)", fmt(median(cp$p)),
                        fmt(min(cp$p)), fmt(max(cp$p))),
        note = sprintf("ClusterSignificance permutation p, median over %d tests; large p means not separable",
                       nrow(cp)))
    } else {
      tibble::tibble(placeholder = "cluster_p", value = "NOT RUN",
                     note = "ClusterSignificance absent or the test failed")
    }
  },
  # Seam test. Reported as median and range like everything else pooled, and
  # only over the phenotypes that actually had a join to test.
  {
    s <- dplyr::filter(seam_tbl, is.finite(ks_seam))
    if (nrow(s))
      tibble::tibble(
        placeholder = "ks_seam",
        value = sprintf("%s (%s to %s)", fmt(median(s$ks_seam)),
                        fmt(min(s$ks_seam)), fmt(max(s$ks_seam))),
        note = sprintf("median across %d phenotypes, %d joins tested in total",
                       nrow(s), sum(s$n_joins)))
    else
      tibble::tibble(placeholder = "ks_seam", value = "NOT RUN",
                     note = "no phenotype spanned more than one block")
  }
)

nice_kable(placeholders, caption = "Values keyed to the manuscript placeholders.")
```

## What this comparison does and does not settle

Both methods are scored identically above, so the numbers are comparable as
measures of how much the synthetic data resemble the real record. That is the
only question they answer.

They do not settle the question the paper is about. The GAN emits its raw trace
and its `Channels` column together, so its labels are a network output; the
diffusion pipeline is handed its labels before it starts and never touches them.
A GAN record could match the real data better on every metric here and still be
the less useful training set, because a downstream idealiser trained against it
is being scored on another network's opinion rather than on truth. If the GAN
wins on similarity, say so plainly and make the ground-truth argument on its own
terms.
